speakers.side_vw_horn_voice: A Voice Like a Hunting Horn

npcs.name: Warden Mirwen Thistledown
npcs.greet: Somebody in this city is bleeding sap and lying about it. If you smell green on anyone's hands, you tell me first.

npcs.name: Faelinor Hart-in-Hand
npcs.greet: Horn, sinew and bone, friend, and not a splinter of living wood. I'd swear to every bow on this rack before the Silvenar himself.

npcs.name: Tanglewyn
npcs.greet: My father leads the best hunting party in Grahtwood. They're nine days late, and I've stopped counting on my fingers because I ran out.

npcs.name: Thrandir Quickstep
npcs.greet: Do you hear horns? No? Good. Good. Nor do I.

npcs.name: Lucia Ennio
npcs.greet: My ancestor marched into Malabal Tor with nine hundred men. I would like to know what he marched out with.

npcs.name: Spinner Hathel
npcs.greet: Don't ask me for a story. I told one I shouldn't have, and now it's telling itself.

npcs.name: Lady Aranwen Ivyhelm
npcs.greet: Woodhearth needs someone to speak for its trees. The Treethane only speaks for his purse.

npcs.name: Gwilin Sweetrot
npcs.greet: Rotmeth, friend? Aged in a guar's belly, and twice as honest as anything the Altmer pour.

npcs.name: Feast-Master Elorin Velvetleaf
npcs.greet: Every guest at my table eats well. That is my only rule, and I keep it.

npcs.name: Old Ilwe Mossfoot
npcs.greet: Mind the spriggan-bark in that basket. It bites, even dried. So does the tree it came off.

npcs.name: Spinner Ollanwe
npcs.greet: I had a story about my mother once. It's gone. Not forgotten. Gone, like a pulled tooth.

npcs.name: Marcus Dorvel
npcs.greet: They won't let me see him. My own brother, and they tell me he belongs to a hunger older than the Empire.

npcs.name: Headwoman Enwe Fernsong
npcs.greet: If you came from the Khajiit wagons, tell their caravan-mother we can count arrows as well as she counts coin.

npcs.name: Rashazi the Caravan-Mother
npcs.greet: This one sells sugar, silk and sense. The Bosmer only ever buy the first two.

npcs.name: Elder Faenruil Bitterleaf
npcs.greet: Speak softly here. The dead are listening, and so am I.

npcs.name: Jirr
npcs.greet: Jirr is not lost. Jirr is hunting. Dellin is helping. Mostly.

npcs.name: Dellin Fernsong
npcs.greet: Don't tell my mother. Unless we win. Then tell everybody.

relics.name: Curl of Jaqspur Heartwood
relics.desc: A pale ribbon of living wood, still sticky with sap. Whoever cut it had a very sharp knife and a very sure hand.

relics.name: Notched Tally-Stick
relics.desc: One row of notches counts bows sold. The second row only makes sense if you are counting trees.

relics.name: Hunter's Bone Toggle
relics.desc: A coat-toggle carved with the mark of an Elden Root hunting party. It was lying in the ashes of a cold fire.

relics.name: Misknotted Rite-Cord
relics.desc: A Spinner's cord of nine knots. The ninth is tied tighter than the rest, as if by a hand in a hurry.

relics.name: Bundle of Stripped Spriggan-Bark
relics.desc: Dried strips of bark tied with a cord and tagged with an apothecary's mark. Some of the strips still twitch.

relics.name: Mask of Woven Antler
relics.desc: A face of shed antler and living vine. It is warm, and it breathes slightly when held near the mouth.

relics.name: Gambling Marker
relics.desc: A bone chit promising four hundred drakes to Cassian Dorvel, signed in a flourishing hand: Gaenor Bitterleaf.

relics.name: Root-Choked Welkynd Stone
relics.desc: A blue Ayleid stone wrapped in fig roots that grew around it on purpose. It hums a tune you almost know.

relics.name: Blooded Hunting Horn
relics.desc: A horn of black antler with a name scratched along its bell. The name is Thrandir Quickstep, crossed out, and yours written under it.

relics.name: Feast-Master's Guest Book
relics.desc: Names of guests at Elorin's open table. Beside one name each new moon, a different hand has drawn a small red cup.

relics.name: Bottled Story
relics.desc: A stoppered vial of ink that whispers in a Spinner's voice when shaken. It smells of old paper and low tide.

relics.name: Satchel of Bottled Stories
relics.desc: Dozens of ink vials, each labelled with a name. One of the labels reads Ollanwe, in Ollanwe's own hand.

relics.name: Legate Ennio's Field Diary
relics.desc: A Legion diary swollen with damp. The last pages are written very neatly, by a man who believed every word was justified.

side_vw_flayed_grove: A dozen jaqspur trees stand stripped to the pale heartwood, bark peeled away in long careful sheets. They are still alive. Sap runs down them like sweat.
The cuts are not a woodsman's. They are a craftsman's, taken along the grain, choosing only the straightest wood.
side_vw_bog_lights: Small lights drift between the reeds, just at the height of a lantern held by someone walking slowly.
Come in, come in, the water's warm. He came. They all came. He was always so easy to call home.
side_vw_bog_wakes: With the wispmother gone, the fog thins. Four hunters lie curled in the reeds, breathing, eyes open, hearing nothing.
One of them, an older Bosmer with a grey braid, keeps whispering the same name: Aelwen. Aelwen. Aelwen.
side_vw_empty_lodge: The Ninth Root lodge is grown from three living trees, its doorways shaped by centuries of coaxing. Every door is torn open from the inside.
Bowls of cold meat sit half-eaten on the floor mats. Claw-marks run up the walls, too high for any wolf.
side_vw_den_hunt_voice: Prey that walks into the den. The knot said until hunger ends. I am hungry still. I will always be hungry.
My son tied this knot. Tell him the Hunt is grateful. Then lie down. It is easier.
side_vw_lirr_speaks: The glade goes quiet. A spriggan taller than a house-tree unfolds from the largest trunk, moss sliding from her shoulders like a cloak.
Another little hunter. Do you carry a knife for bark too? Your kind peels my children like fruit and sells their skins in the city.
Find the peelers and the one who buys from them. Bring me a name, and I will stop taking foragers. Bring me nothing, and I will take more.
side_vw_echo_flatters: The carved antlers on the stone run with green light, though no sun reaches them.
There you are. I have waited a long time for someone strong enough to carry my face. I was the Wilderking. Greenshade remembers me.
My mask lies at the Thornless Throne. Wear it, or give it to the one who carved this stone. Either way, I will be king again.
side_vw_hollow_oak_truth: Inside the hollow oak, old carvings cover the heartwood: a man in a crown of leaves, binding an antlered shape with vines, sealing its face in a mask.
Beneath, in Bosmeris worn almost smooth: Here the King put the Wild's hunger into a face, and the face into the dark, so it would never be worn.
Clever little carrier. Too clever. Then I will wear you instead.
side_vw_lamps_sing: Blue light leaks up through the fig roots. Somewhere below, a voice is singing in a language older than any tree in Malabal Tor.
One more root. One more, little digger, and the stars will shine on Heliandil again. Sing with me while you dig.
side_vw_horn_speaks: The shrine's stone is wet with fresh blood, though nothing lies dead on it. Far off, a horn answers a horn.
Run, little quarry. Run well, and you may yet become the hunter. Run badly, and you will feed the Huntsmen, and the Huntsmen are always hungry.
side_vw_cellar_found: Under a burial mound outside Woodhearth, a door of new oak has been set into old earth. The smell of rotmeth gives way to something sweeter and much worse.
Rows of feast-chairs line the dark. Each has a name carved on its back. The newest is still sticky.
side_vw_ink_trail: The ink stains lead from Falinesti to the shrine like drops from a leaking quill. At the altar, they pool into a single word, written and rewritten until the stone is black.
More? You've brought more? No... you are not a Spinner. You are only a reader. Readers are such poor meals.
side_vw_legate_greets: The dead graht-oak has been hollowed into a fort, its roots shaped into palisades and its trunk cut with arrow-slits. Moss has grown over the Legion eagle.
Citizen! At last, the relief column. The tree-folk broke the truce and murdered my cohort in their sleep. Avenge us, and the Ninth will rest.

quests.title: Sap on the Bowstring
quests.pitch: Someone has been cutting jaqspur in the groves north-east of the city. Not windfall: living trees, stripped to the heartwood and left standing like flayed men. The Wardens blame the Imperial traders, and the traders blame us. Find the cutters before this turns into a war over firewood.
quests.desc: Warden Mirwen Thistledown of Elden Root told me someone has been secretly cutting living jaqspur trees north-east of the city, a crime against the Green Pact. She asked me to find the cutters before the city finds someone else to blame.

objectives.text: Find the flayed jaqspur grove north-east of Elden Root
Take a curl of cut heartwood as proof
objectives.journal: The spriggans were not angry at me. They were angry at anyone holding a blade near those trees, and I happened to be holding one.

objectives.text: Follow the drag-marks to the cutters' camp
Deal with the jaqspur cutters
Bring down the cutters' captain
objectives.journal: Sorrel Quickhatch laughed while she bled. She said her employer's name was on half the bows in Elden Root, and that the Wardens bought from him too.

objectives.text: Search the camp for the buyer's tally
Confront Faelinor the bowyer in Elden Root
objectives.topic: Your tally-stick counts trees, Faelinor.
objectives.reply: Horn bows crack in the wet. Did you know that? Every hunter in this city draws a bow I made, and every one of them came home because it didn't break. I gave them jaqspur and called it bone. Y'ffre has been very patient with me.

choices.label: The Wardens will hear this from you, not me.
choices.reply: Then I'll walk to them myself. Take the last bow on the rack. It shouldn't hang in a liar's shop.

choices.label: Burn every bow you have and leave Elden Root tonight.
choices.reply: Exile. Kinder than the Wardens and crueler than you know. Take the last one. I never could burn it.

objectives.text: Report to Warden Mirwen
objectives.topic: The cutter's employer was Faelinor.
objectives.reply: Faelinor? I carry one of his bows. I have carried it for eleven years. ... Then I suppose I've been breaking the Pact for eleven years and calling it piety. Leave me. I need to unstring something.

quests.outro: The jaqspur thief of Elden Root was Faelinor Hart-in-Hand, the city's most pious bowyer. When I told Warden Mirwen, she unstrung her own bow and set it on the floor.

quests.title: The Lantern Fen
quests.pitch: My father's party went south after a herd of graht-elk. Five hunters, eight days' meat. They were due back the night the lights started showing over the southern fens. Find their camp. If they're dead, I want to know how. If they're not, I want to know why.
quests.desc: Tanglewyn of Elden Root asked me to find her father's hunting party: five hunters who went south of the city after elk and never came back.

objectives.text: Find the hunting party's last camp south of Elden Root
objectives.journal: The fire had burned down to nothing, but the meat was still on the drying racks. Bosmer hunters do not leave meat.

objectives.text: Search the camp
objectives.journal: Five sets of footprints left the camp walking in a line, heel to toe, toward the fens. Nobody walks like that unless they're following something.

objectives.text: Follow the footprints into the Lantern Fen
Wait in the fen for the lanterns to come out
Put out the drifting lanterns
Destroy the wispmother calling the hunters
objectives.journal: Before she came apart, the wispmother said a name, gently, like a mother calling a child in for supper. The name was Tanglewyn.

objectives.text: Bring the news to Tanglewyn in Elden Root
objectives.topic: Your father's alive. So are three of the others.
objectives.reply: He stumbled in an hour ago, mumbling about lanterns. He won't say anything else. What was out there?

choices.label: It was your mother. Aelwen. She wanted him back.
choices.reply: Mother drowned in those fens when I was small. ... Then she wasn't drowning. She was waiting. Thank you for telling me. I think.

choices.label: Only a wispmother. It's dead now.
choices.reply: Good. Father keeps saying Mother's name in his sleep, but he always has. Thank you for bringing him back.

quests.outro: I found Tanglewyn's father and three of his hunters in the Lantern Fen, called there by a wispmother who had once been his wife. One hunter never came out of the reeds.

quests.title: A Knot Tied Wrong
quests.pitch: Slavers from the sea took three of my clan this spring. The Ninth Root begged me to call the Wild Hunt, only a small one, only for the raiders. I tied the rite-cord myself. I tied it wrong. The Hunt took the raiders, and then it kept going, and it took the clan that called it.
quests.desc: Spinner Hathel of Woodhearth helped his clan, the Ninth Root, call a small Wild Hunt for revenge. He tied the rite-cord wrong, and the Hunt turned on the clan that called it.

objectives.text: Go to the Ninth Root lodge in Greenshade
Drive off what's left of the clan
objectives.journal: They still had clan tattoos under the fur. I tried not to look at them too long.

objectives.text: Find the rite-circle where the Hunt was called
Take the rite-cord from the circle
Bring the rite-cord to Spinner Hathel
objectives.topic: Here's your cord. The lodge is empty.
objectives.reply: Empty. No... look here. The ninth knot. I tied it until hunger ends, when it should have been until the debt is paid. Debts end. Hunger never does. Not in Valenwood.

quests.outro: The Wild Hunt Hathel called is still running because of one wrong knot. He says it will not stop until its heart stops.

quests.title: The Hunt-Heart
quests.desc: Hathel says every Wild Hunt has a heart: the first hunter to change. If the heart stops, the Hunt ends. He did not want to tell me whose heart it was.

objectives.text: Ask Hathel who leads the Hunt
objectives.topic: Who was the first to change?
objectives.reply: My father. Gwaeren, clan-chief of the Ninth Root. He took the cord in his teeth before anyone else could. If there were a way to bring him back, it would be in the knots, and there isn't. Please be quick with him.

objectives.text: Track the Hunt to its den in southern Greenshade
Hold the den until the Hunt returns at night
Fight off the returning Hunt
Still the Hunt-Heart
objectives.journal: When the Hunt-Heart fell, every howl in Greenshade stopped at once. For a moment Gwaeren had his own face again. He used it to say his son's name.

objectives.text: Tell Hathel the Hunt is over
objectives.topic: The Hunt is over. Your father said your name at the end.
objectives.reply: Then he knew it was me who tied it. Of course he knew. What do I tell the cousins who were away when it happened?

choices.label: The truth. You tied it wrong, and you sent me to end it.
choices.reply: A Spinner who lies about his own knot shouldn't spin anything. I'll tell them tonight, at the fire.

choices.label: Tell them the slavers cursed the rite. They'll believe it.
choices.reply: They will. And I'll know. That can be my knot to carry.

quests.outro: I stilled the Hunt-Heart in its den in southern Greenshade. It had been Gwaeren, chief of the Ninth Root, and his son tied the knot that made him.

quests.title: Mother of Thorns
quests.offer: Who peels bark off a spriggan?
quests.pitch: Never you mind who. There's an old spriggan in the glades west of here, older than the city, big as a house-tree. Mother Lirr, the foragers call her. Three gatherers dead this month, torn up like roots. The hunters want her dead. I want to know why she started, after three hundred years of minding her own business.
quests.desc: Old Ilwe Mossfoot of Falinesti told me an ancient spriggan matriarch called Mother Lirr has started killing foragers. The hunters want her dead; Ilwe says she wants to know why.

objectives.text: Find Mother Lirr's glade west of Falinesti
objectives.journal: Mother Lirr let me walk out of her glade. She told me to bring her the name of whoever buys her children's bark.

objectives.text: Find the bark-strippers' camp
Drive off the bark-strippers
Put the half-peeled spriggan child out of its pain
objectives.journal: Rootwrath had been tied to a stake with its own vines and peeled a strip at a time, as the orders came in. It fought me because it could no longer tell one soft-skinned thing from another.

objectives.text: Take the bundle of bark waiting for delivery
Confront Ilwe about the mark on the bundle
objectives.topic: This bark is tagged with your mark, Ilwe.
objectives.reply: Spriggan-bark cures the marsh-cough. Half of Falinesti breathes because of my basket. I never asked where they peeled it, because I knew. Now what, hunter?

choices.label: You stop buying, and I make peace with Lirr.
choices.reply: And the marsh-cough? ... I'll find another cure, or I'll be the one coughing. Go on, then. Tell her it was me.

choices.label: Lirr killed three foragers. I'm going to finish her.
choices.reply: Then my basket stays full, and I'll sleep badly. We all pay for the cure somehow.

objectives.text: Return to the glade and settle things with Mother Lirr
objectives.journal: Whatever I chose, the glade answered with thorns. Lirr's children had their own opinions about peace.

objectives.text: Return to Ilwe in Falinesti
objectives.topic: It's done in the glade.
objectives.reply: The foragers went back out this morning, and nobody's been torn up. I'm told the trees seem easier. Here. A fang from the Pact-wardens' old armory. I traded for it years ago and never felt I'd earned it. Neither of us has, but you're closer.

quests.outro: Mother Lirr's killings began with Ilwe Mossfoot's bark basket. The bark-strippers are gone, and the glades west of Falinesti are quiet again, one way or another.

quests.title: The Antlered Echo

find.text: A standing stone sunk in moss, carved with a crown of antlers. Beneath it, freshly cut: The King under the roots will answer the one who wears his face. Go to the Mossed Stone. - A.

quests.desc: Near Woodhearth I found a standing stone carved with antlers and a message signed only 'A.', promising that a buried king would answer whoever wore his face.

objectives.text: Go to the Mossed Stone north of Woodhearth
Take the antler mask from the Thornless Throne
objectives.journal: The mask breathed against my hands all the way back. I did not put it on. I wanted to, which worried me more.

objectives.text: Find 'A.' in Woodhearth
objectives.topic: You carved the stone. What's in this mask?
objectives.reply: The last Wilderking. He'll speak for Woodhearth's trees through whoever wears him, and the Treethane will have to listen. If you doubt it, go to the Hollow Oak west of the stone. The old carvings there will vouch for him.

objectives.text: Read the carvings in the Wilderking's Hollow Oak
Destroy the Antlered Echo
objectives.journal: The Echo was never the Wilderking. It was the hunger he caught and masked. It had been calling itself a king for so long it nearly believed it.

objectives.text: Tell Lady Aranwen what she nearly wore
objectives.topic: The mask held the thing the Wilderking imprisoned, not the Wilderking.
objectives.reply: It promised me... it said the trees would kneel. Of course it did. That's what hunger would promise. What do I do with it now?

choices.label: Break it. Here, in front of you.
choices.reply: Do it. Quickly, before I ask you not to.

choices.label: Keep it, empty, to remind you what you nearly became.
choices.reply: A dead mask on the mantel. Every guest will ask about it, and every time I'll have to tell the truth. Fair.

quests.outro: The voice under the Mossed Stone was not the Wilderking but the hunger he had chained. Lady Aranwen of Woodhearth will have to speak for the trees in her own voice.

quests.title: The Mandate's Due
quests.offer: What hunger are they talking about?
quests.pitch: My brother Cassian hired on as a caravan guard with the Bitterleaf clan. They say he fell fighting bandits, and that under their Meat Mandate his body is theirs to honor in their own way. I'm not here to insult anyone's gods. I only want to know he really died the way they say.
quests.desc: Marcus Dorvel, an Imperial in Arenthia, asked me to visit the Bitterleaf clan, who claim his brother Cassian's body under the Meat Mandate. Marcus doubts Cassian died the way they say.

objectives.text: Visit the Bitterleaf clan's camp west of Arenthia
Speak with Elder Faenruil Bitterleaf
objectives.topic: Marcus Dorvel asks after his brother.
objectives.reply: Cassian fell defending our wagons at Wagonbreak Ridge. The Mandate is meant for fallen enemies, so that nothing of them is wasted. We rarely grant it to a friend. My son Gaenor insisted Cassian would have wanted the honor. The body rests under the rite-hides until the third night.
objectives.journal: Elder Faenruil asked me to keep my voice low near the rite-hides. I did not look under them, and I did not need to.

objectives.text: Look over the skirmish ground at Wagonbreak Ridge
Search the ridge
objectives.journal: There were no bandit arrows on the ridge. Only Bitterleaf fletching, and a gambling marker in the grass where a man had fallen.

objectives.text: Show the elder what you found
objectives.topic: Gaenor owed Cassian four hundred drakes. Every arrow on that ridge is Bitterleaf.
objectives.reply: The Mandate is a promise to the dead, not a grave to hide a murder in. Gaenor left at dawn, for the old hide south of here. Bring him back to me. Or do not. The clan will understand either.

objectives.text: Find Gaenor Bitterleaf at the old ridge hide
objectives.journal: Gaenor swore the Mandate was his to bend because he was the elder's son. He bent it right into a grave.

objectives.text: Tell Marcus Dorvel the truth in Arenthia
objectives.topic: Cassian didn't die fighting bandits. Gaenor killed him over a debt. The elder has disowned his son.
objectives.reply: Murdered. Over four hundred drakes. And now the clan wants to finish their rite as if he were one of their own?

choices.label: They mean it as honor. Cassian was their friend.
choices.reply: I don't understand it. I don't think I'm meant to. But I'll stand at the edge of their fire and say his name, so at least one Imperial voice is in it.

choices.label: I'll ask the elder to release his body to you.
choices.reply: Thank you. I'll take him home to Skingrad. The worms there are at least Colovian.

quests.outro: Cassian Dorvel was murdered by the son of the clan he guarded, and the Meat Mandate was nearly used to hide it. Elder Faenruil would not let the Mandate become a lie.

quests.title: Lamps Under the Fig

find.text: A cracked Ayleid urn half-swallowed by fig roots. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth, a hunter's note: The blue lamps under the strangler fig sing at night. Brannoc went down after them. Brannoc came back up singing, and he has not stopped.

quests.desc: Outside Falinesti I found a hunter's note in a broken Ayleid urn, warning of singing blue lamps under a strangler fig and the hunters who went down to them.

objectives.text: Find the sinkhole under the great strangler fig
Get past the singing hunters
objectives.journal: They kept humming even as they fought. The tune was not a Bosmer one.

objectives.text: Follow the roots down to the Ruins of Elnalorne
Pry the root-choked welkynd stone from its socket
Silence Heliandil the Root-Bound
objectives.journal: Heliandil had been singing to the Bosmer for a hundred years, teaching them to dig him out one root at a time. He was three roots from free.

objectives.text: Bring the stone to a Spinner in Falinesti
objectives.topic: This stone has been singing hunters into the ground.
objectives.reply: Ayleid lamps. My grandmother called them the stars that eat songs. I'll sink it in the deepest pool in the river, where nothing with ears can hear it. Thank you for not keeping it. Most do.

quests.outro: Under a strangler fig outside Falinesti, an Ayleid lord named Heliandil had been singing Bosmer hunters into digging him free. The fig can keep its roots now.

quests.title: Cubs of Two Clans
quests.offer: Are you expecting trouble with the Khajiit?
quests.pitch: My boy Dellin is gone, two nights now, and the Khajiit wagons rolled in the day before. Their caravan-mother swears her people took nothing, then turns around and accuses us of stealing her own kitten. If nobody blinks by tomorrow, there'll be arrows in those wagons. Find my son. Quickly.
quests.desc: Headwoman Enwe Fernsong of Arenthia's son is missing, and so is a Khajiit kitten from Rashazi's caravan. Each side blames the other, and the border is close to blood.

objectives.text: Speak with Rashazi the Caravan-Mother
objectives.topic: Enwe's son is missing too.
objectives.reply: Missing? Or hidden, so the Bosmer can say Rashazi's people took him? ... Jirr has been gone two nights. Jirr has also been talking for a month about Old Ash-Stripes, the senche that took our dray-beast in the eastern hills. Perhaps this one should have listened better.

objectives.text: Follow the children's trail into the eastern hills
objectives.journal: Two sets of small footprints, one with claws, walking side by side. Someone had drawn a very bad map in the mud with a stick.

objectives.text: Find Old Ash-Stripes' den
Kill Old Ash-Stripes before it finds the children
objectives.journal: Two small heads popped up from behind a boulder as soon as the senche fell, both of them cheering.

objectives.text: Talk to the cubs
objectives.topic: Your families think you were stolen.
objectives.reply: Stolen? Jirr and Dellin are hunting! We were going to bring back the skin, and then nobody would fight, because nobody fights heroes. Jirr will run ahead and tell Rashazi. Was it a good plan?

objectives.text: Bring Dellin home to Arenthia
Return Dellin to Headwoman Enwe
objectives.topic: Your son and Rashazi's kitten went hunting Old Ash-Stripes. Together.
objectives.reply: Together. With a stick-map. Rashazi is laughing so hard at her wagon that her guards have put their bows away. What do we do with the pelt?

choices.label: Split it between both clans.
choices.reply: Half a pelt each. Rashazi will want the bigger half. This once, let her have it.

choices.label: Give it to the children. They earned it.
choices.reply: A Bosmer and a Khajiit sharing one blanket. There's a Spinner's tale in that, someday.

quests.outro: Arenthia's border feud ended with two children, one stick-map and a dead senche-tiger. Headwoman Enwe and Rashazi are not friends, but they now agree on something.

quests.title: Quarry of the Horn

find.text: A log totem crowned with a stag's skull. A fresh strip of hide is nailed beneath it, painted in blood with a single word, and the word is your name. Somewhere north, a horn sounds once.

quests.desc: Near Hircine's shrine in Grahtwood I found a totem with my own name painted on it in blood. Someone has made me the Huntsmen's quarry.

objectives.text: Go to the Shrine of Hircine in Grahtwood
Wait at the shrine for the moon to rise
Survive the Huntsmen's first chase
objectives.journal: They came at me from three sides at once, and then from a fourth I had not known was there. I ran, and then I stopped running.

objectives.text: Run to the old killing-ground at Stagfall
Turn on the master of the Huntsmen
objectives.journal: Varkhalen died laughing. He said the Huntsmen never choose their quarry. Someone in Elden Root had traded my name for his own.

objectives.text: Take Varkhalen's blooded horn
Find Thrandir Quickstep in Elden Root
objectives.topic: Your name is scratched out on Varkhalen's horn. Mine is written under it.
objectives.reply: Twelve years ago I swore myself to the Hunt for an arrow that never misses. This season it came to collect. I only needed a better runner than me. And you are one. You're alive. Doesn't that count for something?

choices.label: Blow the horn and give him back to the Hunt.
choices.reply: No... no, please, I hear them already...

choices.label: Keep the horn. Nobody is anyone's quarry.
choices.reply: You'd let me keep running? Then I'll run somewhere the horn can't follow. Thank you, Huntsman. That's what they'll call you now, you know.

quests.outro: Thrandir Quickstep sold my name to Hircine's Huntsmen to save his own. I ran the Hunt, killed its master at Stagfall, and decided what the quarry owed.

quests.title: The Open Table
quests.pitch: Not the rotmeth. The guests. Feast-Master Elorin keeps an open table every new moon, and every new moon one of my regulars goes off to his feast and never stumbles back here. Bosmer drink, yes, but we always come home to pay the tab.
quests.desc: Gwilin Sweetrot, a Woodhearth innkeeper, says that every new moon one of his regulars goes to Feast-Master Elorin's open table and never comes back.

objectives.text: Attend Feast-Master Elorin's table
objectives.topic: Gwilin says your guests go missing.
objectives.reply: Guests go home in all directions, friend. Some to the sea, some to the trees. I don't follow them. Sit, eat. You look pale.
objectives.journal: Elorin ate nothing himself. He watched the door a great deal, and his guests very little.

objectives.text: Watch the feast-hall door after dark
objectives.journal: A guest in grey left with a drunk Bosmer on her arm. She did not stumble once on the stairs. He did not stop stumbling.

objectives.text: Follow the guest in grey to a root-cellar outside town
Deal with the cellar's thralls
Destroy the Pale Guest
objectives.journal: Before she died, Ithrelle told me Elorin set a place for her at every feast. She paid for her seat in gold, and he never asked what she ate.

objectives.text: Take the guest book from the cellar
Confront Feast-Master Elorin
objectives.topic: Ithrelle is dead. She had a guest book. You kept her chair warm.
objectives.reply: She paid. Everyone pays at my table, one way or another. I never saw anyone bitten. I only set the chair. ... What happens to me now?

choices.label: Close the open table, or the Treethane reads this book.
choices.reply: Closed. Tonight. Woodhearth will say I've grown miserly, and I'll let it.

choices.label: Pay every family whose son you served her. In full.
choices.reply: That will cost more than she ever paid me. Which I suppose is the point.

objectives.text: Tell Gwilin his regulars are safe
objectives.topic: No more open table. The Pale Guest is dead.
objectives.reply: A vampire at Elorin's feasts. And I kept sending them there with directions. Your rotmeth's free for life, friend. Don't tell the others.

quests.outro: A vampire called Ithrelle had been dining on Feast-Master Elorin's guests every new moon, with a chair he set for her himself. Gwilin's regulars come home now, if not always sober.

quests.title: The Story-Eater
quests.pitch: Spinners carry the clan stories in our heads, every hunter's name back to the Merethic. This month they're vanishing. Not fading. Pulled out. Every Spinner in Falinesti wakes with a hole in their memory and ink on the pillow. Someone is harvesting us.
quests.desc: Spinner Ollanwe of Falinesti told me the stories carried by the city's Spinners are being stolen from their minds, leaving ink stains on their pillows.

objectives.text: Search the Spinners' sleeping-loft for the thief's trace
objectives.journal: Under a floor-mat I found a vial the thief had dropped. It whispered in a Spinner's voice, and the ink inside smelled of old paper and low tide.

objectives.text: Follow the ink-trail to the Shrine of Hermaeus Mora in Reaper's March
Drive off the ink-collectors at the shrine
Descend into the Inkwell Barrow
Destroy Ollo the Ink-Mouth
objectives.journal: The Ink-Mouth had been a Spinner once. He traded his own stories to the Prince of Knowing for favor, ran out, and had been eating other people's ever since.

objectives.text: Gather the bottled stories from the barrow shelves
Bring the stories back to Spinner Ollanwe
objectives.topic: One of these jars has your name on it, in your own hand. You sold it.
objectives.reply: I did. My mother left the clan for a Colovian, and the story of it was a thorn I couldn't pull. A soft-voiced stranger offered to take it for a quiet night's sleep. I didn't know he would come back for the rest of us.

choices.label: Your mother's story is yours. Take it back.
choices.reply: Heavy. Heavier than I remembered. I'll carry it. I'm a Spinner; that's the job.

choices.label: Return the others. Pour yours into the river.
choices.reply: Then let the river remember her. It's better at it than I was.

quests.outro: A fallen Spinner called the Ink-Mouth had been drinking Falinesti's stories for the Prince of Knowing. The first story he ever bought was Ollanwe's own.

quests.title: The Ninth Cohort's Oak
quests.offer: What did he march out with?
quests.pitch: Legate Corvus Ennio led the Ninth Cohort into Malabal Tor in the Second Era to punish a clan for raiding a supply train. None of them came back. My family says the Bosmer slaughtered them under a flag of truce. I'm a scholar, so I'd like to read it somewhere other than my grandmother's mouth. They built a fort into an old graht-oak. I think I've found where.
quests.desc: Lucia Ennio, an Imperial scholar in Elden Root, asked me to find the root-fort in Malabal Tor where her ancestor's cohort vanished, and learn how they really died.

objectives.text: Find the Ninth Cohort's fort in the roots of a dead graht-oak
Fight through the shades of the Ninth Cohort
Find the legate's field diary
objectives.journal: The diary said nothing about a truce. In his last entries Ennio ordered a grove burned with the clan's children hiding in it, to teach the trees a lesson. The trees learned. So did the Ninth.

objectives.text: Lay Legate Corvus Ennio to rest
objectives.journal: The legate insisted he had been betrayed right up to the moment there was nothing left of him to insist with.

objectives.text: Bring Lucia Ennio the truth in Elden Root
objectives.topic: Your ancestor burned a grove with children in it. It's all in his own diary.
objectives.reply: In his own hand. Neat, too. Grandmother always said he had beautiful handwriting.

choices.label: Publish it. The Bosmer deserve the record.
choices.reply: Then that's the history I'll write. Grandmother can disown me. She's threatened it over less.

choices.label: Bury it. Some debts are better left in the roots.
choices.reply: I'll take it back to the oak myself and leave it there. I'll know. That will have to be enough.

quests.outro: The Ninth Cohort was not betrayed under a flag of truce. Legate Ennio burned a grove with children in it, and the forest answered. His descendant now holds the proof.
